title: PASTEL,PAINTING & PRINT INCLUD...
reason: Three framed pictures led by what reads as a Baxter oil colour printed music title page and a bush oil signed 'H. Eyles' (catalogued Harry Eyles); attributions unverified online. Value band is my estimate only.
findings: Five photos of three framed works. (1) A framed sheet-music title page 'The Holy Family': a gilt-bordered arched colour picture of the Virgin, Child and infant St John (looks like after Raphael's Madonna della Seggiola) above 'Admired Sacred Melodies by the most celebrated composers, arranged for the piano forte as solos and duets, with ad lib accompaniments for flute, violin and violoncello', arranger credit at the foot looks like William Hutchins Callcott (the surname ends ...COTT). A small-caps line under the picture, partly degraded, reads 'Printed by G. Baxter, the inventor and patentee of oil colour printing'; if the sheet is genuine that makes it a George Baxter oil colour printed title page of the 1840s to 50s. Publisher imprint at the foot is illegible. (2) A small framed oil on canvas-textured board of a split-slab bark hut with a distant peak and ringbarked trees, signed lower right in cream paint, reads 'H. Eyles' (cursive, fits the catalogue 'Harry Eyles'); the weave is very even and may be canvas board. (3) A framed pastel of a bushman seated on logs by a slab hut and gum tree with haze or smoke; no signature is visible in the exposed corners and the lower edge is under the mount, so an Eyles attribution for the pastel is not supported by the photos. The web search budget was used up, so neither the Baxter imprint nor Harry Eyles as a recorded artist could be checked online; both are unverified.
condition: Title page: toned, with a brown water stain at the top left edge, foxing and a horizontal crease across the right half; framed behind glass in a modern maple-look frame with white mount, not seen out of the frame. Oil: paint surface looks sound with no obvious cracking or loss. Pastel: glazed with reflections, mount slightly tanned, no obvious damage visible but flaking not checkable.
rescore_note: The Baxter imprint is legible on the music title page so it is likely a genuine Baxter print, but it is stained and creased; the H. Eyles bush hut oil and unsigned pastel are decorative Australiana, and neither the print nor Eyles could be checked online.
